text:
Predicates:
City(x) ::: x is a city.
State(x) ::: x is a state.
In(x, y) ::: x is in y.
USState(x) ::: x is a U.S. state.
Premises:
City(billings) ∧ In(billings, montana) ∧ USState(montana) ::: Billings is a city in the state of Montana in U.S.
In(butte, montana) ∧ In(helena, montana) ∧ In(missoula, montana) ∧ USState(montana) ::: The state of Montana includes the cities of Butte, Helena, and Missoula.
City(whiteSulphurSprings) ∧ City(butte) ∧ ∃s (USState(s) ∧ In(whiteSulphurSprings, s) ∧ In(butte, s)) ::: White Sulphur Springs and Butte are cities in the same state in U.S.
City(stPierre) ∧ ¬In(stPierre, montana) ::: The city of St Pierre is not in the state of Montana.
∀x (City(x) ∧ In(x, butte) → ¬In(x, stPierre)) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
∀x ∀s1 ∀s2 ((City(x) ∧ USState(s1) ∧ USState(s2) ∧ In(x, s1) ∧ In(x, s2) ∧ s1 ≠ s2) → (x = bristol ∨ x = texarkana ∨ x = texhoma ∨ x = unionCity)) ::: A city can only be in one state in U.S. except for Bristol, Texarkana, Texhoma and Union City.
Conclusion:
∃s (USState(s) ∧ In(stPierre, s) ∧ In(bismarck, s)) ::: St Pierre and Bismarck are in the same state.
